answer: Randomness-Locked Slot Assignment. Each epoch, a verifiable random beacon (threshold BLS) assigns every registered key a fresh slot in a dune of shards; only assigned slots may act, and assignment is unrevealed until the beacon fires, so attackers cannot precompute placement. Because a sparrow-sized share of keys lands in each active shard, mass-registered identities collide and get pruned. A prism of audit challenges then samples slots, forcing attackers to maintain real liveness per key. Cost: one live, continuously responsive host per surviving identity, plus wasted registrations.
